summary_oneline: Tool-Call Delegate: local tool-calling-only model as a third execution step between PlanToolNode and AgentNode

localization.role: Reference implementation — DelegateToolNode follows this pattern, adding a propose_call step before ToolManager.execute_tool dispatch
Data model the DelegatePlanNode extends — adds instruction, facts, tools list, min_confidence, on_reject fields
Fan-out model reused by delegate nodes — same source/select/concurrency semantics
Registration pattern to follow — ensure_delegate_node_registered for NODE_REGISTRY['delegate']
Extension point — add delegate-specific rules (tool count, side-effect policy, instruction template resolution)
Reusable CEL evaluator for the accept_when gate on delegate proposals
Dispatch target — accepted delegate proposals call this, same as PlanToolNode
Needs new metadata: delegate_safe flag and optional delegate_description
Storage target — delegate results stored here, same path as PlanToolNode

constraints.description: parrot.interfaces.* is a mixins package for bot capability interfaces (aws, database, http, etc.), NOT a Pydantic-contracts home. The proposal's suggested location parrot/interfaces/delegate.py breaks this convention.
constraints.implication: The ToolCallDelegate protocol and ToolSpec/ToolCallProposal models should live in parrot/bots/flows/plan/delegate.py (co-locate with the module they extend), not in parrot/interfaces/.

constraints.description: FEAT-585 (plan-then-execute-hardening, 16 tasks active) explicitly declares changes to bots/flows/plan/ models/validator/guards/compiler as NON-GOALS.
constraints.implication: The delegate can safely extend plan/ files without conflicting with FEAT-585 work. The delegate could later benefit from FEAT-585's checkpointed execution recovery, but it is NOT a dependency.

constraints.description: register_node(name) checks issubclass(cls, Node) and raises ValueError on duplicate names. NODE_REGISTRY is a dict, not a plugin system.
constraints.implication: DelegateToolNode MUST extend Node from parrot.bots.flows.core.node. Registration must be idempotent (same pattern as ensure_tool_node_registered).

constraints.description: The plan-then-execute design doc at claude/handle-only-execution-design.md does NOT exist on disk. The canonical references are sdd/specs/execution-plan-tool.spec.md (FEAT-419) and sdd/specs/plan-then-execute-hardening.spec.md (FEAT-585).
constraints.implication: The proposal's references section needs updating.

constraints.description: PlanToolNode.make_tool_node_factory closes over tool_manager, working_memory, permission_context, plan_run_id, step_mapping — these are runtime bindings, not plan text.
constraints.implication: make_delegate_node_factory must follow the same closure pattern, additionally closing over the delegate pool/backend.

constraints.description: No ToolSpec model exists in the codebase. The ToolManager has ToolSchemaAdapter for Bedrock format adaptation, but no standalone schema-export type.
constraints.implication: ToolSpec is genuinely new, not duplicating an existing abstraction. The schema adapter may inform its design but is not a conflict.

what_is_new: Validator rules for delegate nodes (tool count, side-effect policy, instruction templates)
Proposal trace log for fine-tuning data collection
what_changes: plan/compile.py — to_flow_definition must handle type='delegate' nodes
parrot/tools/abstract.py — AbstractTool gains delegate_safe: bool = False and optional delegate_description: str | None
pyproject.toml — new optional extras for needle and llama-cpp-python
non_goals: Async support in NeedleDelegate (wait for upstream)
patterns_to_follow: PlanNode field structure and Pydantic ConfigDict(extra='forbid') (F003)
CEL guard compilation and evaluation for accept_when (F007)
integration_risks: Needle 3 context window is undocumented — the spike (§10 of the proposal) must answer this before spec
Needle's thread safety is assumed non-reentrant — ProcessPoolExecutor is safe but adds latency; the spike must measure to_thread viability
Fine-tuned Needle returns confidence=None — the accept gate must handle this gracefully (already addressed in §6 of the proposal)
Adding delegate_safe to AbstractTool is a public API change — needs clear defaults (False) so existing tools are unaffected
The 5-tool ceiling per Needle call is a hard architectural constraint — plans that exceed it must split the step, and the validator must enforce this

confidence_map.claim: Plan module (PlanToolNode, ExecutionPlan, ArtifactRef, validate_plan) is landed and working
confidence_map.reasoning: Direct wiki query + file reads confirmed exports, factory, tests

confidence_map.claim: NODE_REGISTRY supports custom node types via register_node decorator
confidence_map.reasoning: Source confirmed; dev-loop nodes already use same pattern

confidence_map.claim: DelegateToolNode can follow the same pattern as PlanToolNode (Node subclass, factory closure, same dispatch path)
confidence_map.reasoning: Architecture is extensible by design — tool type is in config, not hardcoded

confidence_map.claim: parrot/interfaces/delegate.py is the WRONG location — should co-locate in plan/
confidence_map.reasoning: Established convention confirmed by prior finding F012 in FEAT-449

confidence_map.claim: CEL guards from plan/guards.py can be reused for accept_when
confidence_map.reasoning: CEL evaluator is generic; only the variable context changes

confidence_map.claim: delegate_safe flag and delegate_description do not conflict with existing AbstractTool API
confidence_map.reasoning: No existing flags or metadata of this kind; default False is safe

confidence_map.claim: FEAT-585 does not conflict with delegate additions to plan/ files
confidence_map.reasoning: FEAT-585 spec explicitly lists plan/ changes as NON-GOALS

confidence_map.claim: Needle 3 base model will achieve ≥90% accuracy on ai-parrot toolkits
confidence_map.reasoning: Needle is trained on mobile-action datasets; scraping/HTTP/DB tools are out of distribution. The proposal itself marks this as unverified and gates on a spike

confidence_map.claim: Instance pool concurrency model (ProcessPoolExecutor) will achieve acceptable latency at p95
confidence_map.reasoning: Neither thread safety nor GIL behavior is documented. Spike §10 must measure this

confidence_map.claim: The bounded replan mechanism (on_reject: escalate) will integrate with the plan runner's existing error handling
confidence_map.reasoning: ForEach.on_item_error exists with fail/collect/skip modes; escalate would be a new mode, but the infrastructure supports per-item error handling

unknowns.question: Should the ToolCallDelegate protocol live in plan/delegate.py (co-located) or in a new top-level module like parrot/delegate/ (independent package)?
plausible_answers: plan/delegate.py — keeps all plan-related code together, delegate is a plan concept
parrot/delegate/ — if the delegate will be used outside execution plans (e.g., standalone triage)
parrot/bots/flows/plan/delegate/ — subpackage with protocol, backends, node in separate files

unknowns.question: Should the spike (§10) be a standalone task or the first task of the feature's task decomposition?
plausible_answers: First task of the feature — spike results inform later task scope but the feature ID is already allocated
Standalone pre-feature spike — separate branch, results determine whether to proceed to /sdd-spec

unknowns.question: For the Epson use case (§8), is the 5-15% residue estimate based on observed data or a guess?
plausible_answers: Based on observed scraping failure rates from production runs
Estimated from general web scraping reliability metrics
Unknown — needs measurement before the delegate scope is sized

recommended_next_command.rationale: Localization is high-confidence (C1-C7) and the design space is well-explored in the proposal. The spike (§10) gates implementation but not the spec — the spec should encode the spike as acceptance criteria. Two low-confidence claims (C8, C9) are about the backend, not the architecture, and the spec's modular backend design means they resolve independently.
